sentences.text: The genus Haliskia contains only one species, H. peterseni, which is known from a partial skeleton including a skull.
The genus name Haliskia combines Greek words for "sea" and "phantom" or "shadow".
Haliskia is the most complete pterosaur species known from Australia.
Based on comparisons with relatives like Arthurdactylus, the estimated wingspan of Haliskia is 4.6 meters.
The holotype specimen of Haliskia was discovered by Kevin Petersen in November 2021 near Richmond, Queensland, Australia.
The species name peterseni honors Kevin Petersen, who discovered and prepared the holotype specimen.
Haliskia peterseni was formally described as a new genus and species in 2024 by Pentland et al.
Phylogenetic analyses agree that Haliskia is a member of the Ornithocheirae.
Haliskia is classified within the family Anhangueridae.
Haliskia belongs to the subfamily Tropeognathinae.
Haliskia actively inhabited the Eromanga Sea, a large inland sea of Australia.
Haliskia lived between 106.3 and 100.5 million years ago during the Albian stage.
One phylogenetic analysis places Haliskia and Ferrodraco in a clade sister to the Ornithocheirinae within the Ornithocheiridae.
Phylogenetic analyses of Haliskia have produced significantly different results regarding its evolutionary relationships and clade composition.
